latin: Vnumquodque in natura intellectuali habet a sua intelligibili unitate et quod quodlibet sibi uniat, et quod immaculatam ac inpermixtam sibi suam seruet proprietatem.
latin_note: Apparatus: 1486 reads 'habet'' (a typographical error, not 'habetur'); 1487 reads 'habet'. Text follows 'habet'.
translation: Each and every thing in the intellectual nature has, from its own intelligible unity, both the power to unite everything else to itself and the power to preserve for itself its own property unstained and unmixed.
